title: Priv EKS headplane Terraform assembly and upgrade sentry
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a reusable Terraform module (module.headplane) that provisions the Redwood Private control plane for EKS clusters with strong upgrade safety, idempotency, and observability. This module should be the canonical entrypoint for creating the customer-managed control plane resources we call the 'headplane' (control-plane VPC, EKS control plane IAM roles, cross-account KMS integration, etc.) and include hooks for staged upgrades and health gating.

Scope:
- Terraform v1.4+ module compatible with AWS provider v5.x and the EKS module constructs we use.
- Resources: VPC (control-plane subnet set), EKS Cluster resource (control-plane), Node IAM roles for control-plane components, KMS key alias integration, S3-backed state hints, and optional CloudFormation bootstrap for nodegroups used by on-prem connectors.
- Upgrade safety: preflight checks, canary-controlplane deploy (single-az), automated post-upgrade health probes, automatic rollback gate if health regressions detected.
- Health checks: k8s API + kube-controller-manager metrics, cert-rotation, etcd snapshot verification (where applicable), and an exporter that feeds console telemetry (headplane.health.* metrics).
- Observability: emit Terraform-instrumentation tags so the Console can attribute latency/cost, and push CloudWatch metrics and logs to the Console ingest path.

Non-goals: single-tenant hardware provisioning, managed nodegroups tuning, or application workload migration tooling. This is focused on the headplane lifecycle only.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module passes idempotency testing across create/update/destroy cycles in our CI (terraform-plan no drift on second apply).
- Canary upgrade flow (single cluster in staging) documented and automated via a lightweight orchestration script in infra/upgrade-sentry.
- Health probes detect injected failures (simulated degraded kube-apiserver) and block rollout, with an automated rollback plan documented.
- KMS cross-account key rotation supports customer-owned KMS ARN and falls back to a Redwood-managed alias when not supplied.
- PR template and preflight checklist added to repo.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use a thin wrapper around upstream eks module rather than reimplementing EKS resource graph to reduce maintenance burden; wrap with opinionated defaults and forward-compatible variables.
- Prefer explicit state locking with DynamoDB for customers using shared backends to avoid accidental concurrent terraform runs.
- Opted for canary-by-az strategy instead of traffic-splitting because control plane rollout changes are disruptive; canary will validate control-plane components in a single AZ before multi-AZ rollout.
- Health gating will initially use CloudWatch metrics and synthetic k8s probes; long-term plan is to integrate with the Console's SLO/alerting engine.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Module scaffolding and terraform fmt + validate pipeline (ETA: 2025-02-20).
2) Integrate KMS conditional wiring and IAM policy templates (ETA: 2025-02-26).
3) Add preflight validations (vpc/subnet sanity, route tables, endpoint reachability) and CI tests (ETA: 2025-03-04).
4) Canary upgrade orchestration scripts and canary job in CI (ETA: 2025-03-10).
5) Observability hooks and dashboard template (ETA: 2025-03-14).

Rollout and testing:
- CI will include a lightweight acceptance suite that runs against a throwaway AWS account we own for infra e2e tests.
- Chaos tests: terraform apply -> inject control-plane kube-apiserver latency -> ensure health probe blocks canary promotion.
- Manual enterprise customer staging run with Solutions Eng before GA.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Terraform provider breaking changes. Mitigation: pin provider ranges and add an upgrade test job in CI.
- Risk: Canary false positives due to temporary CloudWatch delays. Mitigation: define short stabilization window + require 2 consecutive failing samples before rollback.

Deliverables:
- sources/infra/modules/headplane (module code) + README + examples/ (customer minimal example).
- infra/upgrade-sentry (orchestration scripts and CI job).
- Confluence runbook: "Headplane upgrade playbook" with rollback steps, runbook links included below.

Security review required: true
